headline: Test 1: Portugal, 1441–1486 · 35:22

items.title: 35:22 · Three years later on January 8 1455
items.detail: Three years later, on January 8, 1455, Pope Nicholas V issued a second bull, Romanus Pontifex, awarding Portugal an exclusive commercial and imperial monopoly over all lands and seas south of Cape Bojador and reaffirming perpetual enslavement.

items.title: 35:36 · Right between those two papal bulls in
items.detail: Right between those two papal bulls, in 1453, the ideological text was compiled to order.

items.title: 35:42 · King Afonso V and Prince Henry commissioned
items.detail: King Afonso V and Prince Henry commissioned the royal chronicler Gomes Eanes de Zurara, Commander of the Military Order of Christ, to write the Cronica do Descobrimento e Conquista da Guine, the Chronicle of the Discovery and Conquest of Guinea.

items.title: 35:58 · As the historian Ibram X Kendi documents
36:12 · Describing the August 8 1444 auction at
items.detail: Describing the August 8, 1444 auction at Lagos, Zurara noted that the captives varied widely in skin tone from near-white to mulatto to black.
